title: SPARKLE Training Course

## Introduction

This course builds on introductory infectious disease modelling concepts and gives students practice adapting, fitting, and extending transmission models.

## Sessions

1. [Recap of infectious disease modelling concepts](session_intro_id_modelling/session_intro_id_modelling.qmd)
2. [Adding age structure to SIR models](session_age_structured_models/session_age_structured_models.qmd)
3. [Introduction to spatial models](session_spatial_models/session_spatial_models.qmd)
4. [Fitting models](session_fitting_models/fitting_models.qmd)
5. [Fitting models - Part 2](session_stochasticity/stochasticity.qmd)

## Session 1: Recap of infectious disease modelling concepts

This first session refreshes compartmental modelling, reproduction numbers, and likelihoods. It includes hands-on activities translating between diagrams and equations, explaining model terms in words, interpreting effective reproduction number trajectories, and refitting a simpler model to simulated outbreak data.

## Session 2: Adding age structure to SIR models

This session extends a basic SIR model to include age groups, age-specific susceptibility and infectiousness, and age-specific contact matrices. It keeps the theory light and uses guided coding activities so students can practise changing model assumptions and interpreting the resulting epidemic dynamics.

## Session 3: Spatial models 

This session looks at different types of spatial models.
It is quite a complicated session, introducing important concepts such as travelling waves and transmission on a network. 
It will be run in a much more interactive way to help everyone achieve their goals.

## Session 4 and 5: Fitting models 

The conclusion of our workshop focuses on introducing some important concepts in model fitting. 
Without model fitting we would not be able to determine important parameters such as $R_0$. 
We will introduce both Frequentist and Bayesian inference, with a quick detour into Markov Chain Monte Carlo. 
The aim is to enable you to understand how more complicated models are fit and be able to identify appropriate data sources for your model.
